material_coverage_findings.finding: Waiting-period facts omit that the later-offense/refusal permits last for the balance of the existing one-year revocation, rather than a new full year.

proposed_statements.statement: A sobriety program permit issued during the subsequent-offense or refusal waiting-period pathway is valid only for the remaining portion of the one-year administrative revocation.
A later-offense interlock permit during administrative revocation lasts for the remaining portion of that one-year revocation.
After the refusal waiting period, the interlock permit lasts only for the remaining portion of the one-year administrative revocation.

material_coverage_findings.finding: Only the felony-flight classification was authored; the misdemeanor/traffic/ordinance pathway and nonmoving exception are missing.

proposed_statements.statement: Fleeing an officer to avoid arrest or citation for a Nebraska misdemeanor or traffic infraction, or a city or village ordinance violation other than a nonmoving traffic violation, is a Class I misdemeanor and may also revoke the operator license.

material_coverage_findings.finding: The general juvenile-court rule for an individual without a permit or license is omitted.

proposed_statements.statement: For the handbook’s age-seventeen-and-younger juvenile-court offense rule, an individual without a permit or license is prohibited from obtaining one for thirty days.
